prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: Pixel Wave native-resolution foreground reef sprite row, raw input for deterministic sprite extraction
Input images: Image 1 is the accepted visual identity and exact pixel-density/style reference; Image 2 is the authoritative two-slot layout guide.
Primary request: Create exactly two distinct SINGLE-PIECE coral-rock formations, one complete connected formation centered in each invisible slot. The left formation is a broad naturally terraced reef about two times the height of the ordinary low seabed reef. The right formation is a much larger asymmetric landmark about three times the ordinary low seabed reef height. Each must be one continuous geological silhouette from a wide solid bottom base to an irregular crown—draw each as one purpose-designed mass, never as rocks stacked or pasted on top of one another.
Style/medium: authentic hard-edged pixel art matching Image 1 exactly; same countable logical pixel size, outline weight, indigo-blue rock palette, compact clusters and deliberate stair-step curves; restrained peach branching coral and lavender tube-coral accents integrated into ledges.
Composition/framing: exactly two equal 144x128 logical slots in one horizontal strip; left subject about 80–90 logical px tall, right subject about 105–118 logical px tall; both fully inside their own slot with at least 4 logical px padding; wide solid undersides suitable for overlapping the continuous seabed; no subject crosses the slot boundary.
Scene/backdrop: perfectly flat pure green #00FF00 chroma-key background filling every background pixel.
Constraints: one complete connected opaque mass per slot; maintain native pixel density instead of enlarging smaller art; binary hard edges; no text, labels, grid, slot boxes, shadows, glow or scenery.
Avoid: stacked-rock construction, separate floating patches, detached coral/debris, antialiasing, gradients, blur, painterly texture, fake micro-pixel noise, cropped forms, empty slot, visible guide marks.
